title: Classical Weil filtration and finite-stage transport data
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with base $k_0$, algebraic closure $k$ and geometric Frobenius [def-weil-punctual-weights], a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega:\operatorname{Type}(u+1)$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with geometric schemes in $\operatorname{Type}(u)$. Use the classical lisse adic sheaves [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], their Weil category [def-wf-fundamental-representation], geometric fibre functors [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors] and canonical automorphism pullback comparisons [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. Define the following filtration and transport DATA; this definition asserts no existence of transports. (1) $\mathrm{ZlClassicalFiltration}(r)$ consists of terms $F_0,\ldots,F_r$, quotients $S_0,\ldots,S_{r-1}$, and specified Weil arrows $F_j\to F_{j+1}\to S_j$. At every algebraically closed geometric point the fibre of $F_0$ is zero and the indicated sequence of fibres is short exact (injective, exact, surjective). Allow $r=0$. (2) At a finite coefficient subfield $E\subset\Omega$, define $\mathrm{ZlFiniteFiltration}$ to be the analogous diagram of the actual sf Weil complexes [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], all terms and quotients in the sf rational constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], with zero initial carrier and short exactness in that heart. The same $E$ contains the diagram arrows and both directions of the Weil isomorphisms. (3) Define the classical orbit point recursively by geometric Frobenius, the ordered iterated Weil fibre map with identity at exponent zero, and the classical local operator as the etale path map followed by that ordered product. Define the finite fibre to be $H^0$ of the recorded point complex [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], its extension to $\Omega$ using the actual coefficient inclusion after $\mathrm{ULift}$, and its map on Weil morphisms by the recorded derived stalk and point-section functors. These use the actual common-stage coefficient category and inclusions [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Define $\mathrm{ZlClassicalFibreComparison}(E,K,F)$ to consist of isomorphisms of these extended finite fibres with the classical fibres at every geometric point, intertwining local operators for EVERY positive period $n+1$ whenever the geometric return equality holds: the return path must act on each finite etale cover by precomposition with the specified $(n+1)$st point Frobenius, and the same fibre identification works for all periods. Define classical punctual purity by the modulus equation $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{w/2}$ for every eigenvalue of the resulting normalized closed-point classical local operator, with all permitted normalized return paths. (4) For a normalized classical Weil realization $R$ [def-zl-normalized-classical-weil-realization], a specified classical filtration $F$, a common-stage Weil heart object $G$, a given top identification $e:R(F_r)\simeq G$, and $\iota:\Omega\simeq\mathbf C$, define $\mathrm{ZlFiltrationTransport}(R,r,F,G,e,\iota)$ as one finite coefficient field, one finite filtration model, and Weil isomorphisms from each finite term and quotient to its prescribed realization. Require the two diagram-map equations after coefficient inclusion; a top isomorphism equal to the last-term isomorphism followed by the supplied $e$; zero initial term and short exactness in the common-stage Weil heart; the all-period fibre comparisons of (3) for every term and quotient; naturality of these fibre identifications for each inclusion and quotient map; and equivalence of the common-stage punctual purity predicate of [def-weil-punctual-weights] with the classical punctual purity predicate for every quotient and every real weight. These are structures and defining conditions, not a theorem that every filtration admits such data.
